newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SE Asia, China need 3 pct oil output rise a year.
newsitem.headline: SE Asia, China need 3 pct oil output rise a year.

text.p: Oil production in Southeast Asia and China needs to rise about three percent a year if they are to continue covering their needs demand, Esso Companies in Malaysia chief Philip Dingle said on Tuesday.

Dingle told the annual Offshore Southeast Asia Conference that 95 percent of demand from the the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and China could now be met by China, Indonesia and Malaysia.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
But demand, driven by industrial and population growth and an improving lifestyle, should grow at about four percent a year, Dingle said.
"This would translate into demand of about 15 billion oil equivalent barrels in 2015, of which six billion would be supplied by oil and gas production," said Dingle.
Dingle said fresh supplies were needed to meet the booming demand, if demand was to be met by local production. He said local output currently outpaced demand by 15 percent.
He said Asia was still relatively rich in oil and gas reserves and had subtantial undiscovered potential.
"Total hydrocarbon reserves and potential are well over 200 billion oil equivalent barrels," he said.
"This is still significant enough to easily cover projected demand.. provided these resources can be found and developed economically," he said.
